title: The last quay roll
body:
Late August 1511. Mahmud Shah and his son Ahmad Shah have withdrawn inland toward Muar and Pagoh. The town has fallen. In the lanes, some warehouses still have their safe-conduct banners; others have been looted. At the landing people turn up with bundles, not cargo accounts.

Your clerk brings tonight's list of names and asks where you will take it. A court runner is gathering people bound inland. A boatman is making room for families at the landing.

choices.label: Take the list inland with the court runner
choices.outcome_text: At the first inland halt, your clerk reads the names. A family that lost sight of its youngest at the landing hears which party she left with.

choices.label: Stay at the landing and help families find passage
choices.outcome_text: You turn the berth list over and write families together instead of ships. The boatman leaves with his boat full and a copy of the names.

notes: fact: The Portuguese accounts summarized in the timeline describe Mahmud and Ahmad's retreat toward Muar and Pagoh, the occupation and sack, and some merchants' safe-conduct banners being respected. Accounts differ on the dates of the capture and final sweep and on which ruler held the throne (docs/research/1511-events.md §§1, 4.4; docs/research/people-factions.md §2, research PR #28).

gameplay: The roll, the evacuations, the choice to stay or go and their effects are invented. The city falls in both outcomes; the choice changes whom the shahbandar helps, not the military result or the next campaign state.
